create.name: Vedanta Society of Portland
create.bio:
The Vedanta Society of Portland is an affiliated centre of the Ramakrishna Order in Oregon, with its temple in south-east Portland. Swami Prabhavananda, who went on to found the Vedanta Society of Southern California, began the work in 1925; a line of monks sent from India followed, among them Swami Devatmananda through the Depression years and, later, the long-serving Swami Aseshananda. Swami Chandrashekharananda, who earlier spent a decade at the Vedanta Centre of Sydney, has been swami-in-charge since 2016, and the society marked its centenary in 2025 and 2026.

Its teaching draws on the Upanishads and the Gita as lived by Sri Ramakrishna, Sri Sarada Devi and Swami Vivekananda: one reality, the divinity of every person, and many paths to the same goal. Besides daily worship and vespers, the temple holds classes on the Gita, the Chandogya Upanishad and the Panchadashi, satsangs with visiting monks and nuns, festival pujas, karma yoga and a free Tuesday evening hatha yoga class, with no registration or fee. The society also keeps Holy Mother's House in Portland and a 289-acre forest retreat near Scappoose, with shrines to several religions, that is open to the public. Talks and classes are streamed on its YouTube channel.

free_resources.title: Free Yoga Classes
free_resources.description: A weekly Tuesday evening hatha yoga class at the temple, open to anyone with no charge; donations are welcome.

free_resources.title: Swami Aseshananda's Lectures (MP3)
free_resources.description: Downloadable recordings of talks by Swami Aseshananda, who led the Portland society for many years.

free_resources.title: Temple Events and Festivals
free_resources.description: The temple's calendar of pujas, birth anniversaries of Ramakrishna's disciples, readings after vespers and holiday programmes. None need registration and all are free.

free_resources.title: Video Talks
free_resources.description: A page of recorded lectures and centre history videos, including talks by Swami Aseshananda and the society's Golden Jubilee film.
